chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, from his father, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-'Ijli, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! Inform me about Ismail, whom Allah mentioned in His Book, where He says: "And mention in the Book Ismail. Indeed, he was truthful in his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet." Is this Ismail the son of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)? For the people claim that it is Ismail, the son of Ibrahim.'

He (peace be upon him) replied: 'Indeed, Ismail died before Ibrahim, and indeed Ibrahim was the decisive proof of Allah for the entire period, standing as the owner of a Shariah (law). So to whom was Ismail sent, then?'
I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Then who was it?'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is Ismail, son of Hizqil, the prophet (peace be upon him). Allah sent him to his people, but they belied him, killed him, and skinned his face.'
So Allah became angry on his behalf against them, and He sent to him Asfata'il, the Angel of Chastisement.
He said to him: 'O Ismail! I am Asfata'il, the Angel of Chastisement. The Lord of Glory has sent me to you to torment your nation with various kinds of chastisement, if you wish.'
Ismail said to him: 'I have no need for that.'
So Allah revealed to him: 'What is your need, O Ismail?'

He said: 'O Lord! You took the covenant for Yourself as Lord, for Muhammad as Prophet, and for his successors as Guardianship. And You informed the best of Your creation about what his nation would do to al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) after his prophet.'
And You promised al-Husayn (peace be upon him) that You would send him back to the world so that he may take revenge upon himself against those who did that to him.
So my need from You, O Lord, is that You send me back to the world so that I may take revenge upon those who did that to me, just as You send back al-Husayn (peace be upon him).
So Allah promised Ismail, son of Hizqil, that, and he will return with al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ حِزْقِيلَ: Ismail, son of Hizqil (the prophet identified in the hadith)
key_terms.تَكُرَّهُ: You send him back (referring to return to the world)
key_terms.صَاحِبَ شَرِيعَةٍ: Owner of a Shariah/Law (referring to Ibrahim)

ai.seo_question: Who is the Ismail mentioned in Surah Maryam 19:54 according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) distinguishes the 'Sincip of Promise' in Quran 19:54 as Ismail ibn Hizqil rather than Ismail ibn Ibrahim, noting that Ibrahim was the primary Prophet and Lawgiver. This Ismail ibn Hizqil, after being skinned alive by his people, requested Allah to return him to earth to exact revenge, mirroring the divine promise made to Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) regarding his martyrdom. This establishes a theological parallel between the two Ismails, linking the prophetic lineage's suffering to the Ahl al-Bayt's ultimate sacrifice.
